Summary: An Ode to the Drink of the Gods...
Text:
This Mango Nectar is perfection! It deserves the highest praise, and I feel compelled to be the one to give it.

First, it must be understood that this is a true delicacy and thus it is to be sipped and savored slowly, not gulped down indiscriminately like a can of coke. If you really want to get the most out of this true little slice of heaven, you have to address it unhurriedly , preferably with your eyes closed. It is best served refrigerated and I like to drink it straight out of the can, because even the can feels good, with its slim line and nice heft. It's actually quite a bit heavier than one expects... So, can or glass, take a sip and gently roll it around on your tongue, like you would a fine wine. Feel the thick richness of the nectar, dancing its dance of subtle, rich flavors in the hiddenmost recesses of your taste glands. Remember to breath gently through your mouth and nose too, to get the full effect of the subtle hues of this amazing fruit's aromas. Notice the tiniest little hint of bitterness - it really rounds out the "feel" of the mango. It no doubt comes from the pulp and, without it, this juice would not be nearly as delectable as it is.

Does this sound like poetry to you? Perhaps it seems like it is a somewhat overdone description of a product that is, after all, "only a fruit juice", right? Well, I invite you to try it yourself and see if it is not deserving of every accolade I have ascribed to it and many others I may have missed.

I am having one now and I must add, though it is probably fairly obvious, I feel it enhances my imagination and my creativity too... :)

I HAVE NEVER MET A POTATO CHIP I DIDN'T LIKE. I HAVE NEVER MET A
POTATO CHIP I haven't eaten...except, perhaps, at parties, where I
had to restrain myself from eating all the potato chips laid out,
lest I leave a bad impression with host, hostess, and fellow guests!

Yes, I must admit it. Potato chips, (along with Three Musketteers
Bars -- also reviewed by me for Amazon), are my very, VERY favourite
snack....and have been, since childhood! Being a "P.C.A." (potato-
chip affictionado), has it's down-side...but it also has it's re-
wards. For instance, though I have never smoked, and never been a
drug-addict, I feel I can more easily understand the agony of
oeople trying to "kick" these habits go through, which also gives
me empathy for problems of all other people, all over the world,
as well! (Should a group be formed, called "Potato Chip Addicts
For Better World Understanding"? Hmmm......perhaps not. Then
again.......)

Of course, the most obvious disadvantage to eating potato-chips
is that doing so tends put pounds on the eater of those potato
chips. So -- many manufacturers have come up with "Light", or
"Reduced Calorie" potato chips. As are the potato chips being
reviewed here: PRINGLES LIGHT SOUR CREAM AND ONION Potato Chips.

O.K. -- they taste GREAT! And, although the side of the
package, (printed in both English and Spanish), lists the sodium
content as 190 mgs per serving, (which seems a lot, though right
now I have no other type of potato chip package to which to
compare it), the salt flavour -- though very prominent, (and
delicious!), was not as over-whelming as in other potato chips I
have had. Thus, the thirst brought on by many other potato chips
I have eaten was not as strong. The sour cream and onions in
these potato chips took over much of the flavour-enhancement,
so, I guess, an overwhelming amount of salt was not necessary.
This, as Martha Stewart might say, is definitely a "good thing".
Because, quenching one's thirst, brought on by eating, (other)
too-salty potato chips usually only makes room for MORE potato
chips in one's appetite. So, you might think that these, some-
what less salty potato chips would be easier to stop eating than
other potato chips. Well -- in my case at least -- you would be
wrong. Because -- with OR without a drink in between bites --
they just taste so darn good!

Why then, do I give these potato chips -- which are fat-free,
contain 50% fewer calories than regular potato chips....and which
do taste S O good -- only three stars? Sadly, because of several
of the ingredients listed on the container. (Had I been able to
read these ahead of time, on Amazon, I might have gotten another
type and/or flavour, of potato chip.)

The full ingredient list for these pototo chips is as follows:

Dried Potatos
Olestra, (Olean Brand)
Modified Cornstarch
Maltodextrin and Rice Flour,

Contains 2% or less of
Non-fat milk
Buttermilk *
Sour Cream Solids * *Cultured cream, non-fat milk)
Salt
Onion Powder
Whey
Dextrose
Monosodium Glutinate
Citric Acid
Lactic Acid
Natural and Artificial Flavours
Disodium Guanylate
Disodium Insinate
Polyglycerol Esters *
Mono- and DiGlycerides *
Alpha Topcopheral Acetate (Vitamin E)
Topcopherals (To Protect Flavour)
Vitamin A Palmitate **
Vitamin K **
And
Vitamin D **
....................CONTAINS MILK INGREDIENTS.................
* Adds a trivial amount of fat ** Dietarily Insignificant

What, you may ask, are so many vitamins doing in a package of potato
chips? The answer is that, to make these chips less caloric, (70 calories per ounce), the fairly-new, artifical fat, OLESTRA, is used.
Olestra, (here with the "Olean" brand name), caused a bit of controversy a few years back when it was first discovered. As I remember it, Olestrra
takes fat out of the body, all right -- but if any other food is eaten with it, the VITAMINS in the food, (either treated with, or eaten with, foods made with Olestra), are also flushed out of the body, before they can give any nutrition! So, the FDA has, to the best of my recollection, mandated that vitamins, (mostly artifical, synthetic vitamins) must be added to foods made with Olestra. And ONLY snack foods, such as these potato chips, can use Olestra at all.

MOST of the other ingredients above, are also nothing to smile about: "disodium guanylate"? "disodium inosinate"? The late consumer
reporter, BETTY FURNESS, once advised her viewers, "If you can't pronounce it, don't eat it!" This is good advice! Sadly, however, other ingredients like "monosodium glutamate", and "mono- and diglycerides", have become SO common in packaged foods today, that most people CAN pronounce these words. Without, however, knowing what they actually mean....

Upon first looking at the ingredients, I THOUGHT they also contained
"Cottonseed oil". Re-reading them, for this review, I am happy to report that Cottonseed Oil is NOT present here. (With "Olestra" as an oil, I guess Cottonseed oil wasn't necessaru.) In passing, however, I would like to mention something I read in the excellent consumer book, "The Supermarket Handbook" -- published in the '70s or '80s. This book, by Nikki and David Goldbeck, is truly "an oldie but a goodie"....and is must reading for people who want to be aware of what they eat, even in the 21st century! In it, the Goldbecks state that: "Cottonseed Oil is not fit for Human Consumption." Why? Because cottonseed oil comes, obviously, from the cotton plant. And -- since cotton is usually used for clothes, and not for food, (except for the oil), THE COTTON PLANT CAN BE SPRAYED WITH ALL SORTS OF PESTISIDES NOT ALLOWED TO BE SPRAYED ON PLANTS USED FOR FOOD! I'm really glad that PRINGLES LIGHT SOUR CREAM AND ONION Potato chips do NOT contain cottonseed oil, (as first I thought they did)....but, looking at the facts that stack up against the frying medium that IS used in these potato chips, (Olestra / Olean), one wonders if the manufacturers have just substituted one bad ingredient for another....

PRINGLES does make some very, very good potato chips. The original has the OU of the (Jewish) Orthodox Union, certifying that they are Kosher -- as, also, do several other PRINGLES potato chips, if I remember correctly. BUT ALL OF THESE ARE TNE REGULAR, FULL-FAT VERSIONS. Any potato chip will make you fat, if eaten to excess....but why lose your vitamins at the same time? (Strange things also seem to happen, when one ingests Olean, to the digestive tract...) For my money, (and life!), I think I'll stick to BAKED Potato Chips, and, perhaps, even the regular versions, from time to time, (to save money), of any Potato chips, from now on.

I did, in fact, call up PRINGLES, and mentioned that I'd like to see them make the Baked potato chips I had seen other manufacturers. The gentleman who took my call said he would pass my suggestion on to marketing.

Here's hoping!!!!

Summary: Pretty good, but I still prefer Stevia
Text:
In the last year I've switched from saccharine, NutraSweet and Splenda to more natural, low-carb or no-carb sweeteners. I've read too many bad things about the artificial ones, and my low-carb diet doesn't allow sugar, honey or agave nectar. I'm in love with liquid stevia, because it works equally well in hot or cold beverages, and also bakes well. It's somewhat expensive, but I feel confident that it's not poisoning me.

Nectresse Natural No-Calorie Sweetener is a close second to Stevia in my personal preferences. I found it to be easy to use in measured packets, and has a similar consistency to table sugar. It sweetens well, although I thought it had a strange aftertaste (but some people say the same thing about Stevia). It's also less expensive per serving than Stevia.

I will probably look for this product again, when my box is empty. It's nice to have several options for natural non-caloric sweeteners. But I still prefer Stevia.

Now, though, Chips Ahoy! has launched two new soft chocolate chip cookies:  the one under review here (Chocofudge) and Megafudge.  I think they are both pretty good, but I think the Chocofudge is better.  The Megafudge is almost like a brownie -- as many fudge-style cookies are -- and I prefer a more conventional cookie.  So, if you are thinking of trying one of these Chips Ahoy! cookies, you shouldn't be too disappointed with either one, but I would go with the Chocofudge.  Actually, of the mass produced chocolate chip cookies, I prefer the Pepperidge Farms soft baked Nantucket chocolate chip cookie.

Summary: Quality has diminished over the years, plastic used is toxic
Text:
Many years ago (at least 10 years, maybe more) I remember eating Emerald Honey Roasted nuts on an airplane and I was thrilled and actually excited about the taste. It came in a little plastic bag. I raved to all my family and friends how great they tasted - just the right amount of salty and sweet.

I'm eating some right now, not thrilled. Could just as easily be some generic brand, hardly any sweet at all. I bought this canister at a local supermarket.

If you're into reusing or recycling plastic containers there's good and bad here. If you want to reuse the container you can remove the entire label and you have a tall dark green plastic containers with a screw on lid - the only marking is an impression on the top of the lid that says Emerald.

Problem is, the top is number 5 plastic and the bottom is number 7. Number 7 is the most unhealthy and hardest to recycle plastic there is so you don't want to reuse this for food and your local area might not accept it for recycling. You can use it for nuts & bolts maybe in the garage? But in my opinion it shouldn't be used for these nuts, or any food. Number 7 shouldn't be used at all, ever, should be illegal. Gases leach off of it and into the food and into the air.....

I think I'm going to throw these out now. I got them on sale so it's not too much of a waste. I just realized they use #7 plastic as I was writing this. Had I realized before, I would not have bought them. I'm going to pay more attention in the future when buying things in plastic jars.

~

Plastic #1: This is polyethylene terephtalate, also known as PETE or PET. Most disposable soda and water bottles are made of #1 plastic, and it's usually clear. This plastic is considered generally safe. However, it is known to have a porous surface that allows bacteria and flavor to accumulate, so it is best not to keep reusing these bottles as makeshift containers. This plastic is picked up by most curbside recycling programs.

Plastic #2: This is high density polyethylene, or HDPE. Most milk jugs, detergent bottles, juice bottles, butter tubs, and toiletries bottles are made of this. It is usually opaque. This plastic is considered safe and has low risk of leaching. It is also picked up by most recycling programs.

Plastic #3: This is polyvinyl chloride, or PVC. It is used to make food wrap, bottles for cooking oil, and plumbing pipes. PVC is a tough plastic but it is not considered safe to cook food near it. There are phthalates in this material-softening chemicals that interfere with hormonal development. You should minimize use of #3 plastic around food as much as possible. Never cook using food wrap, especially in a microwave oven. If the wrap is listed as microwave-safe then I would still not let it touch the food while using it in the microwave. #3 plastic is rarely accepted by recycling programs.

Plastic #4: This is low density polyethylene (LDPE). It is used to make grocery bags, some food wraps, squeezable bottles, and bread bags. This plastic is considered safe, but is unfortunately not often accepted by curbside recycling programs.

Plastic #5: this is polypropylene. Yogurt cups and similar wide-necked containers are often made from it, as well as water bottles with a cloudy finish. You'll also find it in medicine bottles, ketchup and syrup bottles, and straws. This plastic is also considered safe, and is increasingly being accepted by curbside recycling programs.

Plastic #6: this is polystyrene, or Styrofoam, from which disposable containers and packaging are made. You'll also find it in disposable plates and cups. Evidence is increasingly suggesting that this type of plastic leaches potentially toxic chemicals, especially when heated. I suggest avoiding the use of #6 plastic as much as possible. It is difficult to recycle and most recycling programs won't accept it.

Plastic #7: This number basically means "everything else." It's a mixed bag, composed of plastics which were invented after 1987. Polycarbonate falls into this category, including the dreaded BPA. So do modern plastics used in anything from iPods to computer cases. It also includes some baby bottles and food storage containers which resist staining. Use of #7 plastic is at your own risk, since you don't know what could be in it. You should dispose of any food or drink related product, especially for children, that is known to contain BPA. I personally also view any other food or drink container made from #7 plastic with a good deal of suspicion. It is difficult to recycle #7 plastic and most curbside recycling programs won't accept it.

To summarize, plastics #2, #4 and #5 are generally considered safe. Plastic #1 is safe too but should not be re-used due to the risk of growing bacteria. Any other plastic should be used with extreme caution, especially around food or drink. The risk is even greater when heating food. For microwaving in particular, remember that microwave safe containers aren't necessarily healthy. They just won't melt. In general, it's better to avoid microwaving plastic entirely and stick to glass.

Summary: AMAZING, but MAKE YOUR OWN (Steps below).

I went to my local indian food store and bought a few bags of powdered / coconut flakes for about $1.50 , threw it in the blender on pulse for a few min, then on high, then on medium, then when it started getting clumped and creamy I set it to low for about 5-6 minutes. Tastes JUST Like it, same consistency, taste, everything. No oil needed,no milk, no sugar, no heat, not even a food processor. The oils come out naturally from the dried coconut flakes/ powder. The butter came out a bit creamier than that in the can, which is a bonus for some considering consistency seemed to be the biggest complain against this product. Summary: When you can no longer breastfeed...
Text:
I have breastfed all three of my children. My first child I breastfed until about nine months. I had to stop at that time because I was pregnant with my second child (surprise!) and my milk dried up. I went to the supermarket to look at formula. I was appalled when I saw that the first or second ingredient was corn syrup. I hightailed it to our local health food store and discovered Baby's Only formula. I took it home, made a bottle, and my daughter guzzled it down. A few months after we started her on formula we were traveling and ran out of the Baby's Only formula and couldn't find a place to buy more. We bought regular formula from the store and she couldn't stand it. I didn't blame her because it smelled really bad compared to Baby's Only.

I was able to breastfeed my second child until he was a year and, therefore, didn't need to switch over to formula. My third child is almost ten months old and I weaned him last night. He has never taken a bottle before. I was concerned that I was going to have a battle on my hands. Well, we got home from the store, gave him the bottle, and he drank it all down. He did well today, too, especially tonight.

I don't know enough about DHA and AHA to comment on what this formula would be like for a newborn/young infant. However, for an older infant (9-12) months, I think that this is a great formula when you can no longer breastfeed.

By having my order reach a certain amount, the shipping was greatly reduced.

Being short of the amount, I decided to try the Gin-Gins, even though I'm not a hard candy kind of guy.A few months later, I was glad I did, however, as one of my new medications gave me dry mouth during the afternoon and when I talked a lot. I was able to put a Gin-Gin in my mouth which kept me from having dry mouth or having to chew on a Ginger Chew during meetings.

I recently had another new med introduced, which has a side effect of nausea, the ginger chew helps calm that down, but isn't always convenient, like at meetings, socializing, or other types of interactions with others. Gin-Gins to the rescue again.

If you're prone to having an upset stomach, I can't think of too many , if any better way to settle that stomach down than a true ginger based product. Gin-Gins are the perfect all around, right in any setting answer.

When taking one out of my pocket, friends, co-workers, or clients, have asked to have one. I've yet to get anything put positive responses for Gin-Gins taste. So for anyone who just likes hard candy, Gin-Gins sure seem a winner with everyone I've shared with.

Try them, (and other fine selections from the Ginger People) you won't be disappointed.

I purchased the Senseo Dark Roast coffee pods for two important reasons.
First, the ease of use and second I REALLY enjoy the flavor of a freshly brewed
cup every time I want one.

Summary: Once a surprise, now a necessity
Text: I first tasted Styrian Pumpkinseed oil a few decades ago while in the service, but on trip to Austria a few years back I had the opportunity to try it again and couldn't believe I'd forgotten what a great flavor it added to foods.  I brought a couple of bottles back to the states, after they were used up, I looked in specialty stores and markets all over the NYC area but with no success.  Finally, I ordered the oil over Amazon.  It arrived quickly and has the same great taste as the product I brought back from Austria.  My only quibble is that I can't get the organic oil that I found over there, but it's pretty much a case of beggars can't be choosers when it comes to finding this oil in the US.  A note to anyone that buys the oil, keep yours in the fridge once you open it as it will go bad if you don't.

Summary: These are ok but not excellent
Text: The skins are tough.  It ruins the flavor.  I have had better from the market.  They are more like chewy raisins than blueberries.  It may be the blueberries I have liked were freeze dried.  These do not compare in quality to the excellent cherries.
I was so happy to see this deal. I recently have been using alot of pumpkin. I was so excited to see an organic product that I could actually afford! I look forward to using it in many recipies.
Terrific quality product, my dog loves them and it is for a good cause. What more could a responsible animal lover want?

Summary: Nice alternative to other sports drinks
Text: I tried this out for the first time last week and was pleasantly surprised. It makes a great change from the usual energy style drink I was used to consuming and it's a lot more healthier.

Out of maybe 4 different Hamburger Helpers I buy on a regular basis, Beef Pasta remains my family's favorite and although I subscribed to it every six months, I think I'll have to change this to 3 months, since we've been eating it more lately.

I've made this with both ground beef and ground turkey and both turn out great. With a nice, beefy taste to it, this is one of the few dishes my picky daughter will go back to for seconds and thirds. My husband said one night that soon I'd need to make two boxes at once, but I think instead I'll just make side dishes to fill people up.

The current subscription price ($7.45 for 6 boxes) makes the price per box come out to $1.24 each box, which is the same as the cheapest sale price I can get at local stores. Usually the sale puts the boxes at $1.50 to $2.50 each, so it's already a bargain with free shipping.

Was my first time purchasing this rice. I thought the jars would be bigger but then again I'm used to shopping at those big club stores. lol . I made some Mexican Rice Pudding with this rice and it came out so smooth and creamy. Just excellent. I was overall satisfied with my purchase. Was delivered quickly.

Gotta love Amazon for carrying this hard to find candy! You can save even more with subscribe and save, but 12 bags is more than enough for now. The candy arrived fast and fresh, will definitely order again.

Chex Mix Select - Chocolate Turtle , 8-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6) The only problem with this product is the bags are too small. There is the perfect blend of chocolate and chex cereal. It's not as bad as eating a candy bar, but hits the spot just as well! What a treat! As a person with an illness that causes nausea from fat, this snack is perfect. I get to enjoy and not get sick from Chex Mix Chocolate Turtle!

Apparently this cat food represents the culmination of exhaustive research into feline nutrition. That may be the case, but good luck getting your cat to eat it.

Feeding this stuff to a finnicky cat is like trying to get a third grader to eat his broccoli. I have to coat it with friskies wet-food to even spark my Bengal's interest, and she still eats around the Core nuggets whenever possible. We haven't had this problem with other dried foods (Royal Canin, et al.) so I can only assume it's the specific taste or texture.

Back to the drawing board.

It took me a while, but I did it. I finally decimated my bottle of EZ-Sweetz. It lasted forever with light to moderate use. I use this in everything. It's great for the discerning low-carber or calorie watcher alike. I personally think it tastes awesome in Kool-Aid. Try it! I'll be placing my second order in the near future!

Summary: Horrible taste. What were they thinking?
Text: I bought this thinking that it would taste like the Kashmiri stuff we are used to. But this one smells bad and tastes worse. It is difficult to even take a small bite of this stuff. Avoid!!!

I have struggled with dry, flaky, itchy dandruff for years! Nothing and I mean NOTHING made it go away. It was so bad that I would have to dust after everywhere I sat! I got this for free through shespeaks and gave it a try. I am so thankful for this shampoo and conditioner. After 3 shampoos my head was the completely clear! That hasn't happened in YEARS! I did try the one specifically for dandruff but those results weren't as good as the regular formula.

This bar tastes very good! The consistency of it, however, is like a rice cake. That kind of stale popcorn texture. But the taste more than makes up for that. High in fiber and protein makes this bar perfect for an on-the-go meal. This bar doesn't keep you full as long as the Regular Kashi GOLEAN bars, but it does curb you appetite for a while.

I wanted to try my hand at making my own bread, so I purchased a bread machine. The King Arthur Flour Baking Companion says according to their tests, the bread machine did the best job kneading bread.

The standard recipe for my machine called for using dry milk powder, so I used SACO. The bread is out of this world!! Once you open a can, then it has to be refrigerated. But the crust and crumb of this bread is so much better than what I expected. I will always keep this product on hand. It is truly a superior product!!
Why would anyone pay 59.99 for a case of 24 when u can buy them at your local Walmart for .99 a piece and it is the same size and ounces??

Summary: Bold, but Not Teeth Jarring Bold. Nice Flavor and a Nice Cup of Coffee.
Text:
Wolfgang Puck French Roast is a nice, bold (not too bold), flavorful cup of coffee. If you like Coffee People Extra Bold Organic, Dark Roast Coffee for Keurig Brewers, 24-Count K-Cups (Pack of 2), then you should like Wolfgang Puck's French Roast.

This French Roast has a deep flavor with a hint of sweetness and a smooth finish - a good choice for a morning cup of coffee.

Recommended.

(Note to Manufacturer: as a consumer, I wish you would use real coffee descriptions(i.e., hints of xxx, smooth finish) rather than fluff advertising like "Bring the aromas of France home with you and "Profitez des bons moments" (enjoy the good moments)!" - what does that really mean? It took me awhile to decide to purchase this coffee because the description gave me zero idea of what to expect).

Summary: Maxwell House Coffee Double Pack from Amazon
Text:
The only difference in my purchase of this produce from Amazon rather than from
my local store is that I do not have to carry it in from the car and the prime
time shipping does create enough decrease in the cost per pound that I see it as
a convenient and economical choice of purchase.
Good long lasting flavorful gum at a great price.Hard to find in my neck of the woods(Long Island).Won't kill ur teeth too!

I use 5 Hour Energy - it's a great little product. But this listing is rediculous. The image shows a box, the description is "2OZ Grape5HR XEnergy", and the price is $28.89 - with free shipping too! Is that a good value? WHO KNOWS?!? Nowhere does the listing tell you HOW MANY bottles are in the box!!
loved the product it is almost as good as folgers and o hve used flogers for years would buy again

Summary: Taste ok, other flavors are better!
Text: So I have had several flavors of these breakfast cookies and have to say this is one of my least favorite flavors.  I think the flavors that are built on oatmeal are better because they taste like they should, like the oatmeal chocolate chunk with raisins are better than these because they taste like an awesome oatmeal cookie with add-ins and not like a oatmeal cookie trying to taste like a chocolate cookie.  The peanut butter ones are three stars too for the same reason.  The oatmeal flavors are all 5 stars!

While reading "How to do Lunch"  I learned of the corn thins and where to order them.  I must say that they are so much better than I guessed they would be.  I have now ordered the second box.  Thank you for carring these.

Summary: Tastes good, but loaded with sugar
Text: The cereal squares were tasty, and stayed crunchy in milk. They had good texture. I took 2 stars off because the name gave me the impression that it was a healthy breakfast choice. I'm in the market for heathier choices, with less sugar due to the fact I'm a Type 2 diabetic. One bowl drove my blood sugar to almost 200!  Please read the ingredient label before you buy!

I was very pleased I found this product on Amazon. I loved it. It was easy to mix up and as a result I used it more often. My disappointment is that it has been discontinued or I would gladly reorder. I gave this product a 5 star rating because of it's taste, ease of use and healthly benefits. I would rather mix this up than grap a soda every time. I hope that this product comes back!

I've ordered almost all of the Asian Entree varieties. Lentil Curry Pilaf is my favorite. The sliced almonds in this dish are a nice touch. I'd highly recommend them to anyone looking for a quick and easy meal option at work or home. I find them to be very filling but I'm a small female so ymmv.

I'd like to note that I haven't had any issues with the dehydrated vegetables. If you are a fan of the Asian Entree line, I'd suggest you give the Lentil Curry Pilaf a try.

Pros: Tastes good, non-toxic, colorful

Cons: Made me fat, can't cut a tomato, ineffective against burglars.

I will give it 5 stars, because stars are cool so there should always be as many as possible.

This is my favorite sugar free mocha instant coffee. It makes a great dessert. I admit to using a bit more product than the instructions recommend. Amazon's price is better than our local grocery store.
Not the best I've tried, but still just fine, and I will continue purchasing it because the container is recyclable, unlike the "boxes" other coconut water comes in.

I love the coffee mild but flavorful.  A great way to wake up and great all day.  Keurig is so easy to use, my elderly neighbor love not fiddling with the paper filters in standard coffee makers. Much easier for him

Zevia Twist tastes so refreshing. The flavor from natural oils of lemons and limes really comes through. I'm a water drinker because soda just never quenched my thirst. But this stuff does. And it's healthy - none of the artificial sweeteners, colors and flavors - chemicals - in all the regular diet sodas. You have to try it to believe it.

Summary: Great Ingredients, Super Messy, and Easy to Choke On
Text: I really, really wanted these to work. They have fantastic ingredients, they taste great, and they're hard... to start off with. Once my 9 month old baby starts chewing on these, they get soft, squishy, and on every single thing they get near. They're perfect if your kid is in a high chair with a bib and can have a bath afterward. The other downside is that they do break off in big chunks and it's easy for the baby to bite off more than he can handle. I'll keep using these when my son is a little older because I think they're probably better suited for an older baby who is teething, rather than someone under a year.
My grocer stopped carrying this product.  I ordered it on line and it arrived promptly and complete.  The oatmeal is delicious and it expires in October of 2014.  Thank you for the great service!
Loved the Keebler assortment!  They are great for kids lunches.  My order arrived quickly and in good condition. I will will buy this proct again!

Summary: Love this BAM of a coffee
Text: I love this coffee. I usually drink Coffee People Jet fuel and still love that but I had a sample of this and now I switch between the two. Sign up for auto delivery. It makes Keurig life so very easy. I haven't had to think about buying coffee for three years. Thanks AMAZON PRIME AND AMAZON SUBSCRIPTIONS!!!

Summary: It doesn't taste like it used to be. Too weak! like 3rd time with water
Text: The last shipping I got, the tea is so horrible. It is like the 3rd time that you put water in...It is so weak. It hardly tasted like green tea that I used to get. I don't know what wrong with it. I ordered 6 boxes/each. So, it took me a few months to finish all 6 boxes. With 2nd package with 6 boxes those a received about a couple months ago, they are so terrible. It almost does not smell like a real tea any more.

I have always used Altoids peppermint mints until I discovered a better mint. Newman's Own organic peppermints. Never will I eat another Altoids mint again after trying Newman's Own Peppermint and they are organic too. Newman's own peppermints are just a better mint.
I was so happy to find this at a good price at Walmart!  I love Bakery on the Main granola.  I mix it with healthy popcorn and it is fantastic!

French Market Coffee & Chicory, City Roast(Dark Roast), 16-Ounce Cans (Pack of 3)

I love coffee, drink about 3 large mugs a day and for over 60+ years have tried nearly every brand and type (Starbucks French Roast, Jamaica Blend and Straight, pure and blended Kona, Sumatra, Costa Rican, Kenya AA, etc., etc.)

This French Roast dark coffee and chicory is a welcome change. When brewed it is very dark, but is extremely flavorful and smooth and I have recently become "hooked" on it. The three 1-pound cans I order every 2 months is really equivalent to 6 pounds as I use half the amount I would normally use for regular coffee.

I have read other reviews which claim that the lower priced French Market C&C Restaurant Blend in the white can is exactly the same as the one in the red can. I have tried both and find this is not the case. The red can C&C in my opinion is the far superior and much richer blend.
As far as a satisfying cup goes it is as good as it gets.

Summary: the best mix on the market
Text: Baja Bob's is a tasty and convenient way to enjoy a 'rita without dealing with all the extra sugar. We have tried the liquid and powdered form and much prefer the single-packet powdered mix, which seems to taste better. And it's convenient! Want a sugar-free 'rita at the beach bar? Just slip a couple packets in the pocket, order a glass of water and a shot of tequila! (I'm sure that most restaurants won't mind if you tell the server that you want a sugar-free drink). This is a fabulous product!

Summary: Without a doubt, the BEST GF pasta out there
Text: I don't normally write reviews, but this product is an absolute must if you need to be gluten free.  It really tastes like regular pasta - we have tried every other possible brand and this is the hands down winner by a mile!  It is expensive, but worth every penny.  I won't every go back to any other brand.  Enjoy!

Exactly what I ordered, prompt delivery.  Completely smooth transaction.  Only observation that I have is that when my office started loving this candy I got it at Target for $7.99 a bag and for this order I paid almost $15.00 a bag.  But my office loves it so here we are!
These are very good gummy bears. This is the second order for this item and I would not hesitate to order again.

These are excellent macaroons and the price is better than I can get them at the store.  My only complaint is that sometimes the bottoms are overcooked/burned.  This has happened in 1 can out of 3.  Great customer service as I ordered 6 and only received 1.  When I notified cs, they shipped another 6 for me right away.

So far, I have thoroughly enjoyed all of the teas in the "zinger" series.  I like Celestial Seasonings in general.  Of course, the tea bags have no strings and that is something of an annoyance, but other than that, the teas are tasty and enjoyable.  Zinger really is a great description of the product.  It has a surprising and deeply flavorful taste and an aroma to match.  It is a great option for those who enjoy herbal teas.
I love the craberry / pomegranate combination.  They're good.  Wish i could find them in the store more often! Great fast snack or breakfast.
Kay's cinnamon pretzels have great crunch and just enough sweetness. The protein/carb balance is comparable to Medifast. I love being able to buy Minnesota-made.

Summary: Add a can of Tuna and whalla
Text: Excellent product. Throw in a can of tuna and it is a meal!

I love this produce and so does my family. It is great for those who are gluten free/limited as well as those who need to limit milk.  I add a little bit of applesause to the mix and it keeps moist longer.

i don't drink coffee, but love tea, and these are wonderful to add to a nice, warm, steamy cuppa.  just a hint of flavor and no "off" taste, nothing chemical or metallic.  just a wonderful boost that makes a good thing even better.  i'm looking forward to trying the other flavors, too.  caramel, yum.  i think i'll combine them.  might even throw in a french vanilla to see what kind of concoction i can manufacture.  :D

This is the best cocoa ever for hot chocolate. It has a strong chocolate flavor and a little bit goes a long way. I've tried many other quality brands but find Droste's pleases me the most. My opinion is totally subjective, of course.

I do not recommend it for cooking and baking. Too strong for fudge and cakes. That's fine. A one-use product is okay with me.

Summary: Puts Standard Fruit-Flavored Sodas To Shame.
Text:
The Izze sodas/fruit juices are quite good. They're a bit more expensive but put the standard fruit sodas to shame. They are, after all, 70% fruit juice and shouldn't even be compared to conventional fruit-flavored sodas. I've now tried two, the first was Blackberry and the present is Pomegranate. Personally, I like the Blackberry a slight bit better but the Pomegranate is outstanding. It's tart. I like than. No sickly-sweet sodas for me! The taste is good and nowhere near the taste of pure pomegranate juice. That's okay. It's a nice refreshing drink with a little bite to it and no added sugar. This stuff is excellent. I think I have two more flavors to try.

Gary Peterson

Funny to think one can have a "favorite sardine brand" but I do and these are it.

Not too salty, lots of fish per can, and olive oil is tasty. I mash the lot up with hot sauce and eat it all. Or I dump it on a salad and dress with a little balsamic on the top. Not very fishy and a great product. I get them on subscribe and save every few months and suggest them to all my paleo-diet friends.

This is canned beans. It may well be that the ingredients are above average, but it still tastes like canned beans. And it is NOT low salt, in fact a can has 600 mg of sodium. It would be very helpful to have the usual info from the actual product with any foods listed on the site. Only a few has it.

My puppy loves these bones! Definitely one of the better purchases I've made to satisfy her need to chew! The different flavors are also nice.

UPDATE! 2 weeks later, she is no longer interested in the brown or white hard bones.... she gobbled up the edible bacon one.... I'm not too thrilled about the purchase anymore.

Summary: the only jarred baby food my son ate
Text:
From 6 month to 12 month, my son barely ate any solid food. He was so picky. We tried many different flavor from various brands and this was the only baby food that he'd actually finish the whole jar. I didn't expect him to like this since it has very green vegetable scent to it, but I guessed it wrong.
Now he is 18 month old and he is a pretty healthy eater. His current favorite seems to be tofu, but he still loves corn, zucchini, brown rice and carrot which are the ingredients of this. I highly recommend to try this baby food.

Also, Earth's Best makes not only the best baby foods but their toddler foods are fabulous as well. My son doesn't really like any snacks from Gerber brand, but he likes most of the products from Earth's Best. Their foods taste great(even for us adult) and so good for you too.

I add this sauce to many dishes.  My favorite is pizza; it transforms the common pie into a real experience.  The larger jars are wonderful; all I can seem to find at the local supermarket are the small ones.

Summary: Really Great granola!! Wonderful! Exceptionally Good!
Text: I tried the French Vanilla Granola made my Golden Temple, from a bulk store and "fell in love" with it.  It was so good that the store supply was out quite frequently... apparently  I wasn't the only one who thinks this Granola has exceptional taste.  I was thrilled to find this product on Amazon.  I purchased this 6 box Pack a couple of weeks ago and 4+ boxes have been throughly enjoyed thus far.  If you like Granola and French Vanilla is a flavor you enjoy... you have to try this Granola!

Summary: OK, but needs to be cheaper!
Text:
My husband loves French Roast and does have trouble with acid after drinking coffee. This would be a great benefit to him but the cost would prevent us from buying it.

The flavor was still too strong for me but then I like really light coffees. I tried it first without creamer and didn't like the taste. I added 1/3 cup of water as I usually do for any coffee and some sugar free French Vanilla Creamer. Then it was fine for me.

I think we would buy it if it was sold at a cheaper price. Kudos for the company for making low acid coffee though.

Summary: Healthy, but cat won't eat it
Text:
My cat ate it once, because it was new, but won't touch it now.
He loves the Blue Buffalo Wilderness Duck recipe, and the ingredients in the Felidae seem to be similar, but he just doesn't like it.

I wish Amazon would carry the Blue Buffalo Wilderness Duck again.

I made a batch of this an ox muesli with 1/2 milk & 1/2 yogurt and put it in the fridge to sit and absorb.  It came out total mush - did not hold up as muesli is supposed to.  Try bob's red mill muesli instead - it's awesome!
This box contained a lot of decaf & coffee that is not extra bold.  The name of the product has "Extra Bold" in it.  This was a bait-and-switch, without question.  Do not purchase this product.

Summary: Not Hot at All - Very Mild Curry
Text:
If you google: "Indian chicken curry recipe" - you will find one of the best chicken currry recipes right at the top. I use this Rajah Mild Madras Curry Powder in the recipe and it turns out fantastic. I've made it numerous times now and we always serve it with peach chutney which really makes it delicious. This curry powder has a full flavor but the recipe I use still calls for cinnamon, paprika, grated ginger and garlic. You also add in tomato paste, yogurt and coconut milk. After you make the sauce you just cook pieces of chicken in the boiling sauce for ten minutes and your meal is ready. The ingredients in this curry powder include: Coriander, Turmeric, Mustard, Bengal Gram (Black Chickpea), Cumin, Chilli, Fenugreek, Black Pepper, Garlic Powder, Salt and Fennel.

~The Rebecca Review
What a refreshing tasting beverage...Unlike anything I have tasted before....The juice and carbonation mix great together...

Our pediatric dentist recommended this gum to my 5 yr old daughter. My kids love it and it's a better alterntative to some of the other "sugar" treats on the market.

I highly recommend it!

I love this food. It smells pleasant. My Ragdoll Mix Garfield has a really sensitive tummy. She would also eat so fast that she would just barf up anything she had eaten. Not to mention she's a very picky eater. It's not the case at all with this food. Both of my kitties love it! It slowed Garfield down and forced her to chew and no more crying in the litter box, or running though the apartment with... anyway it was scary... Sadly I have two cats, I'm on a low income, and as much as their health is my to priority. I can't afford to buy this for them anymore. T_T Really great food though. I will buy it again when I can.

I can't believe I found this on Amazon.  What a great thing!  I'm a nurse and work five 12-hour shifts in a row, so I don't have the time nor the inclination to eat.  I live on Carnation Instant Breakfast.  It's soooooo good and has the vitamins I need.  It tastes like the richest chocolate milk ever.  It came in a 3-container pack, so I've got enough to last quite a while.  I highly recommend this.

We found this product while on vacation in South Carolina. Once we got home, we found it wasn't available in our town so, I went to Amazon.com and sure enough, there it was! It's a wonderful snack that 'grows on you' the more you eat. We were so pleased that once we ordered it, it arrived within 48 hours! Great service and cheaper than making a 45 mile drive, one way, to get it.

I am new to sugar-free eating so I have had a string of disappointment while trying to find some decent s/f treats.  I have looked everywhere and I cannot seem to find these cookies in the Midwest, however, I found them while visiting in Alabama.  I bought three boxes, taking the chance that I may not like them.  I am so glad that I did.  They are 50 calories per cookie, so they are not a low calorie treat, but they are just as delicious as the original.  I read another reviewer who had some inconvenient intestinal tract reactions.  These cookies did not affect me in this way at all.  I gave them a 5-star b/c in my opinion this is a superb product.  I will be sad to run out of my boxes, but they are on my Amazon Wish List!

Good quality quinoa that has already been washed thoroughly to remove all the saponin, so that it isn't bitter when cooked. The 4 bags come in a nice little box that can be used as a storage tray in your kitchen cabinet. Price is a little steep, so cheaper options may be available at your local grocery store, but the convenience of home delivery is nice!

I found this mix at the Ft Myer Commissary.  I looked for this product last time I visited the commissary and could not find it.  So here I am online looking and found it here.  I could eat this all day.  I've tried several different snack mixes, but most have too many pretzels.  This has a very nice balance of flavors and textures -- and not a lot of pretzels.  I'm stocking up!!

Love this stuff! My dog had the most AWFUL gas before I switch his food. He was getting pro pac mini chunk, I think it's because I got the corn out of his diet. I mix his food with Earth Bourne Holistic primitive too.
This is the best lower calorie hot chocolate I have tasted.  It is very chocolatey and leaves no after taste.

I love this tea in fact I just ordered more it awesome I'm now a lifelong customer of Mood & Mind I recommend all their products. It's such a powerful relaxation calming tea I actually have been drinking it quite a bit. Loved and love it.  I actually love this tea so much I've been making it almost every night and I feel so wonderfully relaxed and just happy mellow All Smiles Tea has brought a big smile to my life.

The Kraft Velveeta Ultimate Cheeseburger Skillets Dinner is quite good. I actually like this better than Hamburger Helper. It's even easier to prepare in my opinion. It's rich, creamy and of course very cheesy. In other words, it's delicious. :)
The only downside is I found it to be a bit salty. Maybe I'm hypersensitive because I don't normally eat foods that are high in sodium content. Everyone's palate is different and perhaps you may not find this to be the case at all. However, those who are sensitive to the amount of sodium in their food, you might agree.

Even so, I'd still recommend this product if you're looking for a quick, easy and tasty meal. The kids will probably like it. I know the adults I had taste test this thought it was good as well.
A very nice looking chrome finish carousel that looks great on our kitchen counter!  We like the larger 35 cup capacity.  The carousel moves easily and the base is sturdy.
I would loose my job if I did'nt keep this stuff available to the coffee drinkers here.  Better stock these all the time.

Summary: I never got used to the taste ...
Text:
It seems like, no matter how long I work with this stuff, I never get used to the taste.

I like shredded dried coconut, fresh coconut, and even the lukewarm putrid watery liquid found in the center of a coconut which is sold in high priced cans at Whole Foods, but somehow coconut milk is kind of ... whatever.

In conclusion: Do you like free shipping? Do you like coconut milk? Do you like cans? Well here it is. And good luck.

I've had this variety of tea from other sources, so I have an idea what it should taste like. When I opened the bag, my nose was assaulted by a strong smell of turpentine - I thought it was the packaging, so I moved it into a plastic storage tub. The brewed tea tasted equally of turpentine. I did find that if you leave the tea out in the air, the taste and smell dissipates, but keeping it for any length of time in a closed container causes the turpentine taste/smell to return. Even aerated, the tea has a very grassy taste to it.

Maybe I got a bad batch, but I will not buy a Numi tea again after this bad experience.
This product is excellent.  I signed up for case deliveries every two months.  Please see that deliveries continue.  Thanks very much.  JASH

This tea is really good for the type of tea it is.  A friend mentioned how this was the best tea she's ever tried so I gave it a shot.  Unfortunately. I tend more towards flavored teas, therefore the 4-star rating.  In my opinion, the Ahmad Peach & Passion Fruit Black Tea cannot be beat.  That is by far my most favorite tea.

Terribly waxy chocolate pieces that all sunk to the bottom of the bowl while the flakes floated on top.  The flakes seem to have a chocolate flavoring added to enhance the experience but those disgusting chocolate pieces made me gag and I wondered what I was eating...!  Alone they were nearly tasteless and I'll never purchase again.  Yuck!

I am familiar with Aguapanela as I grew up in Southamerica. Pannela tastes very similar to the one we used to make home. It is also ver refreshing and I was trilled to know that it preserves all the nutrients from the cane juice. Being all natural, with no preservatives it was also a nice benefit of this drink. I would recommend it for all Southamericans and those that enjoy healthy and different drinks.

I was skeptical about buying Vanilla beans, or any packaged foods, over the internet. Gluten-Free Flour Tortillas
MAKES 6-8 TORTILLAS

1 cup white rice flour
1/3 cup potato starch
1/3 cup tapioca flour
1/3 cup fava bean flour
2 tsps xanthan gum
1 tsp baking powder
1/2 tsp sugar
1 1/4 tsp salt
2 TBs vegetable or other shortening
3/4 to 1 cup warm water

Combine all of the dry ingredients, then cut in or work in the shortening using a pastry blender or two knives or your hand.
Add the warm water, starting with 3/4 cup and mix well.
Continue to add water until a soft, cohesive dough is formed.
Heat a comal, tapa or griddle to medium heat. Then, form a ball of dough into a flattened disk, cupping the outside edges a bit to form a round.
Using a bollilo or rolling pin, roll into a round disk about 1/8 inch thick and about 8 inches in diameter or to your preference.
Bake one at a time on a hot griddle until the surface bubbles. Turn only once, the first side should have brown flecks.
Bake until the second side has slightly browned - should brown in a very short time.
Keep warm in a tortilla keeper or wrapped in a cloth until served.
Note: Will freeze in a sealed plastic bag for up to three months.

Reprinted courtesy of The Jane Boutel Cooking School, Alberquerque, New Mexico.

Summary: One of the better drink mixes I've tried
Text:
I'm not sure what a Mango is supposed to taste like since I've never had one, but I've had a lot of Peach's and this has some real Peachy flavor to it! It says on the bottle that it has "24 servings" in it. But it doesn't say how much a serving is. It took a few tries of squirting some of this out of the little bottle to notice that if you keep squeezing it will only squirt so much out. I thought that it measured each squirt to be the same amount, and maybe its supposed to, but it seems to vary a little from one use to the next. And after buying a few other flavors each bottle seems to squirt a different amount so there is no way to really measure how much you use. But making each little squirt as close to the same as I can, for a 12 oz. glass of water with a little ice it takes 3 or 4 squirts of this to get the flavor about right, without making it too strong or too sweet. So far I've used 18 squirts out of this one bottle and got six 12oz. glasses out of it. The little bottle feels to be just about empty, maybe enough for one or two more 12oz. glasses, so its going to come out pretty close to 24 squirts out of the little bottle. So for the number of servings that they claim it has in it, 24, the servings would only be a little over half a cup, 4oz. to 6oz. I don't know about you, but to me that is not a serving to drink. So they are being very misleading about how many servings there is in the little bottle and its really only 10. Maybe a couple more if you mix it really weak.

Other than not actually making as many servings as it claims, it is a pretty good drink. It has a nice Peachy flavor that is closer to the real thing, without being the real thing, than any other drink mix I've had. If you use too much it gets a bit on the sweet side but you really have to use a lot. I've been using the Crystal Light drink mix for a long time but I think I've found something that's better than it is and I'm going to be using this for quite a while. Even if it is misleading about how many "servings" you really get out of the little bottle. Besides all that, its really pretty good with a shot of spiced Rum in it too! [;-Þ

I bought this dog food because the bag showed pictured of veggies and chunks of meat, and with a name like "Beneful" I thought I was purchasing a nutritious brand of dog food. My dogs did eat this food, but after reading the ingredients I completely regret purchasing it and feel just awful for feeding it to my dogs. The first three ingredients are Ground yellow corn, chicken by-product meal, and corn gluten meal. How disgusting is that?! The main ingredient is a corn filler. One thing my vet told me a while back that I never forgot: "When you eat corn, what comes out of the other end? The same thing happens with dogs." Basically, corn cannot be completely digested, it is just a filler and causes dogs to actually eat more to feel full, poop out more, and retain less nutrients. The only meat in Beneful at all is a by-product, its not even a real meat! By-products are the stuff leftover once all the actual meat is harvested. We're talking beaks, chicken feet, eyeballs, even chicken poop! I would not recommend this product to anyone, for any reason, ever. It is an absolutely awful dog food. I can't believe the pictures of veggies and full chunks of meat on the bag can be allowed to be on the packaging of such a disgusting product; it is very misleading and should be considered false advertising.

I recommend to stay far away from Beneful, and most Purina products. When purchasing a dog (or cat) food, the most important thing to consider is the first 3 ingredients; just make sure those first three are decent ingredients that you would eat yourself. Now that I know what to look for, I usually buy my pets foods such as Blue Buffalo, Halo or Wellness.

Summary: Ahmad Earl Grey Tea, 100TB ~ The Most Exquisite Earl Grey I've Ever Tasted
Text:
I first came across Ahmad Earl Grey Tea a number of years ago, while I was visiting a friend who lives out in Seaford, Long Island (NY). I was waiting for her to meet me in a mall, there, & I just happened into a Mideastern grocery-deli to browse and look at the great variety of exotic foods & spices they had for sale.

By & by, I started getting thirsty & asked the shopkeeper whether he had cups of hot tea for sale. He showed me the varieties of tea they had & I chose Ahmad Earl Grey Tea, since Earl Grey has been my favorite ever since I was introduced to it back in the late '70s by an English friend of mine, who would prepare it with milk or cream & sugar or honey.

Well, I had had excellent cups of Earl Grey tea in the past -- Twinings, Bigelow, Island-Rose & others -- but nothing I had previously tasted had fully prepared me for the sublimely fragrant, yet delicate & nuanced bouquet of aroma & flavor that literally "took me by surprise" upon my first sip of Ahmad Earl Grey Tea... aroma & flavor that was not just a simple one-dimensional taste but one that seemed to unfold as you drank it, revealing delightfully unexpected subtleties, layers & shades of enchantingly fragrant aromas & flavors.

Surprisingly, the high quality of the tea leaves & the bergamot used to impart the flavor were clearly distinguishable to me in the tea's unmistakably delightful yet delicate aroma, not only when opening the box of 100 tea bags, or the individual envelopes containing the bags of tea... but quite detectable, in the tea bag itself, even after having made a cup of tea or two, making me wonder whether they might have discovered some very effective, secret manner of infusing the bergamot aroma into the tea leaves, or the tea bag, such that the aroma didn't dissipate after having made a cup of tea, or even while standing on the shelf of the grocery, as I've noticed sometimes happens with lesser grades of Earl Grey tea.

In any event, after such an incomparable experience with Ahmad Earl Grey Tea, it is the only Earl Grey tea that I choose to drink, unless I happen to be out somewhere where it is, unfortunately, not available.

It is at such times that I am so appreciative to have come across Ahmad Earl Grey Tea.

Though I often purchase it at Mideastern food markets, for instance in Astoria, Queens, where it is readily available at rock-bottom prices & fresh from the importers, nevertheless, for those of you who are too far away to do so, the fact that it is available here on Amazon.com is already quite a boon, especially if you order a number of packages of it to lessen the impact of the shipping charges.

If you do order Ahmad Earl Grey Tea & try it, I'm quite sure that you'll find that it soon becomes for you, as it has for me, "a most exquisite delight, definitely not to be missed!"

Summary: Wish I had known more about Kombucha
Text: After reading that some people have issues with Kombucha tea, I Googled it and read some more. I recommend that others do the same before drinking it. I am sure that Yogi Tea produces their Kombucha in a careful environment, but it can cause health problems. It also does not appear to be appropriate for people with Candida despite some claims. It contains alcohol, sugars, fungi, yeast and molds, and a study showed that it did not improve symptoms of people with Candida. I've been drinking it almost daily and have been having unexplained stomach aches lately and will try eliminating this tea to see if it helps, now that I know more. Again, read up on Kombucha and make your own informed decision.

Summary: Bewley's (and Barry's too) are my favorites.
Text:
This blend was my first experience drinking Bewley's tea. I found that I liked it very much. Loved it,that is. There was one cup of it that I felt was probably the best tea I'd EVER tasted, but I've never been able to duplicate the flavor of that one cup! --Have found that my tea is best if I make it in a pot instead of a cup and carefully follow basic classic good tea-making instructions, i.e., pour boiling water in the pot to prepare it beforehand, then when tea-water is boiling, pour out the hot water from the teapot, put in tea-bags (1 to each 8 ounces of water), pour in the boiling tea-water, place the lid, let steep 4 or 5 minutes. It seems that Tea made in a pot comes out mellower, less harsh-tasting than in a cup. Still, I keep getting different flavor results with each different pot of tea I make. Very mysterious problem. Maybe I need to time the process precisely with each cup or batch and note down the results of each different timing, then see if the timing produces a consistent result every time.

(I used to flavor my tea with honey, but now I prefer Xylitol sugar substitute which is mild but satisfying, has less calories, and possibly is healthier.)

I also love Barry's Tea. Both Bewley's and Barry's are my super-favorites. (Not available in my grocery so am happy that I can order both brands through Amazon and can get super-saver no-shipping-fee.)

Text:
They were discontinuing these at my local grocery store and after purchasing this... I can kind of see why. I know that this isn't going to be an eating experience akin to fresh or even frozen tuna steaks, but I expected a little more than this.

Taste-wise, there's not a lot of mesquite flavor. This was more salty than anything else. It's not a horrible flavor, but when you compare it to some of the flavors that abound in the bagged/canned/ready-to-eat tuna market this just falls short. I've tasted far better.

Texture-wise, my tuna was rather dry in texture. I wasn't expecting it to be like the tuna you cook up yourself, so this wasn't really a deal breaker for me. Bagged tuna is sort of a 50/50 type of thing as far as texture and dryness goes, although I did note that there was a substantial amount of water in the bag.

Overall this is just one of those items that is just a disappointment. It's not bad enough to where you'd feed the remaining bags of tuna to the stray cats or chuck the rest of your meal in the trash, but it isn't good enough to where you can see yourself going out of your way to buy more of it in the future. I've got a couple more of these tuna steaks in different flavors, so I'll see if those are any different. I wouldn't say that you should avoid this, but it wasn't really something I'd recommend rushing out and buying either.

Summary: China not ready for prime time
Text:
Someday, it will be safe to buy food products from China. Today is not that day. Everyone knows China is very poorly regulated and the Chinese people suffer from all kinds of side effects as a result. Why should that problem and uncertainty be exported? The only way to manufacture in China is for the outsourcing company to STRICTLY and CONTINUOUSLY audit the manufacturing process -- because we cannot rely on their native legal and regulatory controls to ensure a safe product. Trio is not Apple Computer. They can't afford to scan the manufacturing all the time.

I had a Trio bar yesterday - first time - and so I wanted to buy more. But I'll have to think twice about this product until they bring manufacturing back to the USA or at least to a country with a recognized high manufacturing standard. Summary: A decent cup of green tea, even better iced
Text:
While I wouldn't describe myself as a tea connoisseur, I am a regular tea drinker. I like both green and black teas. I buy the Kirkland Signature Green Tea Matcha blend especially for brewing iced tea: 5-7 tea bags in cold water left overnight in the refrigerator, remove tea bags, and serve with or without ice. I find it needs no sweetener or lemon. Tea bags left longer than 24 hours will make the tea bitter and the matcha sediment can also become bitter.

There are other teas I like better, such as a Gen Mai Cha or a high quality Jasmine tea. For the price, the Kirkland brand is just fine and reliably available at Costco.

I have such a love/hate relationship with licorice, and I had to try this one, I just had to. Licorice in tea is one of my favorite things of all time, and the Licorice Mint tea from Red Leaf Tea is a must for me when I'm sick. And while I love allsorts, any other licorice candy is not for me. I just think it's vile. Every Easter my mother would gleefully sit by as I sorted out all of the black jelly beans from my basket. She was the only one in the family who liked them. Is there anything more gross than popping what you think is a purple jellybean into your mouth, only to discover it was a horrible, horrible, licorice one? Blegh! But allsorts....mmm. They've become a bit of tradition in our family. They're impossible to find in Tennessee, so when I'm sending a package to my folks I always include Coffee Crisp for my mom and allsorts for my dad. That is, if I can keep myself from eating them all before the package goes out! Trust me, it happens more often than I care to admit.

I kept eyeing this tea, adding it to my shopping cart and then removing it in favor of another flavor of matcha, adding it back to my wishlist. I finally bit the bullet and I'm here to find out if this is an allsort or a black jellybean.

It's not a black jellybean at all! It is a lovely sweet licorice that soothes the throat and makes me unbelievably happy. I was very scared of this blend, but those fears were unfounded. It is delicious and definitely one I need to keep around for when I'm sick but I have to deal with work anyway. Completely lovely. It's not really an allsort either, it's the licorice I've come to know and love in teas. I should have expected that, but I was scared by the picture on the website.

Licorice tends to polarize people. You either love it or you hate it. I'm one of those who loves it, but my wife is one who hates it. If it's in a tea, she can taste it, and it bothers her. But for me...oh, I love it and this matcha is beautiful in the balance of flavor to matcha. I want to make a large mug of this, but I have other matchas to taste and review!

I tend to have good luck when it comes to vending machines, and always come across one that has something stuck in a rung, free for the taking once I shake it a few times. Recently I spotted a pack of these almonds in one, shook it out, and gave it a shot. I hadn't tried them before since they were in the 'healthy' vending machine where the cheapest thing is a fiber cookie for nearly one Abe Lincoln. But hey, when almonds are free, I won't turn them down. Almonds are already great on their own, and these suckers add other great ingredients to the mix, making for an excellent snack.

You get the usual crunchy almonds, apples, flax seeds(!), balsamic vinegar, sea salt and red peppers. Flax seeds make everything better, in more ways than one, and I'm really glad that snack foods are starting to feature these more. The apple taste is faint but you definitely get it as soon as the almonds hit your tongue, and the red peppers...something that I've actually never had in my life, aren't strong at all. That was my only real concern with this snack when I was opening it. Despite my heritage, I've never had any kind of spicy foods, but I bit the bullet and I absolutely love these.

As usual with great snacks, the only bad thing is the price, but Amazon has a pretty good deal on them. While 'soledad' might mean 'loneliness' in Spanish, you'll be able to overcome that feeling as long as you've got a pack of these babies around. Buy some immediately...or shake 'em out of a vending machine.

Summary: Flavor is good, but Eww, texture!
Text:
This review is for the texture snobs in the world. As others have mentioned in their reviews, the flavor is great and the ingredients/nutrition are better. Hold on, though: there's a "but" coming.

Remember the flavored instant oatmeal we ate before we knew what "organic" or "gluten" meant? Brightly colored "banana" bits held onto their fake yellow color and their cubic shape long after the hot water mushified the oats for us. We ate fake crap, and we liked it.

We're older and wiser now, and want real bananas: real bananas that we re-hydrate ourselves with our steaming hot filtered water for optimum health and enjoyment.

Except that rehydrated banana bits don't stay in bit form. Nor do they rehydrate to sliced banana consistency. Nay! Rehydrated banana bits taste like delicious, wholesome bananas, and have the consistency of runny snot.

That's right: runny snot.

I love everything else about this oatmeal, but when I want to feel snot run down my throat, I'll go out and contract the common cold, thank you very much.

Based on other reviews, this doesn't throw everyone. Based on other reviews, you might love this oatmeal and shrug off the banana snot texture without a second thought. But if you're a huge texture snob, I thought you might want to know what you're getting into.

I will shudder and finish the rest of my banana oatmeal one snot-filled bowl at a time (unless I can't take it anymore, at which point the food bank gets a wholesome and delicious donation), but I won't purchase this again. I think I'll slice bananas into gluten-free oatmeal the next time I feel a bananas-and-cream craving.

Best of luck with your oatmeal experience, and thank you for pausing to read a different perspective.

Summary: Great Buy and the Price is Right!
Text:
we've been devout Folgers coffee drinkers for over 35 years and never thought we'd switch brands. after my husband had a bout of heart problems, he was told to go to decaf coffee or stop drinking it, which wasn't an option. we started buying the Folgers half caff and he cut back to 2 cups a day. when i bought the keurig coffee maker Keurig B70 Platinum Brewing System i switched to the Green Mountain Breakfast Blend Green Mountain Coffee Breakfast Blend, 24-Count K-Cup for Keurig Brewers (love it) and bought the ekobrew refillable k-cup Ekobrew Cup,Refillable K-Cup For Keurig K-Cup Brewers 2-Pack - BROWN $ GREEN for him and his Folgers half-caff.

on a whim, i decided to buy a small box of the Green Mountain half-caff k cups for him to try. i was very nervous about it because he's such a die-hard Folgers kind of guy. since i don't care for decaff coffee i didn't want to have to drink it if he didn't like it. he took a couple big drinks of the coffee and i finally asked him how he liked it. he said he liked it a lot, and thought it was much better than the Folgers half-caff, it seemed to have a lot more flavor. phew!

in fairness to Folgers half-caff ground coffee, the reason he may think the Green Mountain half-caff has more flavor could be because of how much of the Folgers he used to make a cup. with these refillable k-cups it doesn't seem to be an exact science, so one cup could be a bit stronger or weaker than the next. i think this is what he was saying. because the Green Mountain k-cups are accurately pre-measured, you get the same taste in every cup.

the bottom line is, he loves the Green Mountain half-caff coffee, and we will definitely be buying more of it. i asked him if he wanted to try the Folgers half-caff keurig coffee and he said, "ummm, i don't know". for a hard-core coffee drinker to be ok with that kind of change says a lot about the GM half-caff coffee. as least it speaks to me of how great this coffee is.

My favorite part is that when the hair is dried, you'd never know that any product was used at all. It's so lightweight and soft! It doesn't leave behind any crunchiness or sticky residue. And my hair absolutely looks so much healthier than it used to.

For maximum convenience, I immediately portion out the box of food into smaller plastic containers. I suppose they could stay out, but I stack most of the containers in my freezer. I add COLD water to a container and put it in the fridge overnight. Next morning, it's reconstituted and ready to serve after warming up.

Pricy? Maybe. But keep in mind that 10 pounds of dehydrated turns into much more after adding water. And the quality of this food is worth the price. I strongly believe that eating should be one of the pleasures of a dog's life. What made us think that it's okay to relegate a dog to a lifetime of eating only dry kibble? I hope I can convey how good I feel about my purchase of the AeroGarden. While waiting for the unit to arrive, I visited some websites with some negative things to say. Nothing serious, but little things that once added up may have led me to steer clear of this system.

Let's just say I'm glad I read about it after I bought it. It was delivered early (Thanks AeroGrow), was securely packaged and after reading the ABC instructions, it was setup in no time at all. I estimate under an hour - maybe 45 minutes. That was almost two weeks ago and for the last few days, I've been noticing sprouts poking their heads outside the seed pod labels - 5 so far.

I am impressed with the quality of the product and simplicity of the design. Everything in one neat little package - simple to use - easy re-ordering system whether through the catalogue or online. The prices may seem steep but you're paying for simplicity and convenience - the fact is that it is literally a plug and play system. You need to know how to do some very simple assembly, fill a reservoir with water, empty a couple nutrient packs and plug it in...it couldn't be simpler. The seed pods fit snuggly into the holes in the growing area and the clear plastic caps create a greenhouse effect for each plant.

I'm so impressed with it, I bought a second unit to grow full sized plants.

Clearly I am a big fan of this tea, so I ordered a six pack! The idea was to have a continuous supply for the next few months, gift some and get a lower price per tin. However, surprisingly, the tea, in this particular order did not taste as wonderful as it usually does. Wondering why, I looked for the expiry date. On the box that they came in, it said, best by 2015. Which is great. However, under each tin, there a date stamped, which is February 2001.

I am very confused. The date marked under the tins...are they expiry dates? They don't say so anywhere. And I know from my past experience of purchasing these (the black tea sampler tin for instance), that the bottom of the tin is where they put their expiry date. I am disappointed. After going through about half of the product (I am on my third pack), I don't know that they are returnable. I kept consuming them thinking, well, the next pack (tin of 22 sachets) will be different, better. They are not. I wonder what to do with the three unopened packs.

First of all, remember that they are what they are: sugar-free candies. Sugar substitutes generally create laxative effects, depending on the person, that can range from mild gassiness to, well, let's not get into that. I think more than one piece is safe--at least 3 or 4 in most cases--but it depends on you. And that's not the fault of the candy, it's the territory in general--most, if not all such candies have that effect.

That said, this is one of my favorite diabetic-friendly candies. They taste very much like the sugary ones I ate as a child. Everyone will have their favorite flavors, but the selection they have is bound to be most satisfying; the flavors are good, the taste well-crafted.

The one drawback I found: if left too long, they will start to congeal or melt in the wrappers. One time I ordered them and it took a month or two for this to start happening; another time I ordered them, they were already starting to go.

All told, it's a product I will be buying often over time.

Summary: Not their best product, that's for sure
Text:
I'm a *BIG* fan of the Vitalicious VitaTop products ("maximum nutrition for minimum calories")--especially the Deep Chocolate version--so I was eager to try the BlueBran mix. But I have to say I was disappointed with this product. Don't be fooled by the photo on the box, people! The "blue bran" name is misleading--I found approximately 3 freeze-dried blueberry 'chips' in my batter. You will definitely need to add your own fresh or frozen blueberries to the mix, otherwise you'll just have plain old bran muffins.

Even after I added fresh blueberries to my batter, the end product was not very good--it was gooey and bland, with a weird after-taste. My family usually inhales the Vitalicious products, but these are still in the freezer.

I have two boxes of the mix left, so I'm going to try adding chunks of apple to the next batch, along with some cinnamon to give it some flavor, and see if I get a better result. Bottom line: Skip these and go for the Vitalicious Deep Chocolate mix.

Summary: Different and Pleasant Tasting Tea Beverage
Text:
I have been a tea connoisseur for a number of years so I was pretty excited about trying this Red espresso Rooibos tea. It is definitely pleasant tasting and can easily become a substitute for coffee and tea drinkers who wish to cut down their caffeine intake. Personally I think that caffeine is part of the magic of tea and coffee and drinking these beverages without the stimulant effect of caffeine is like eating chocolate that is not sweet.

Though this tea definitely has a unique appearance and taste, it would be great to have a regular caffeinated version that can be consumed for its taste and stimulant effect.

*** Positive Points: ***

+ Unique taste for a tea
+ claims to have the same antioxidants as normal tea

*** Negative Points: ***

- No caffeinated version for people who like the stimulant effects of tea and coffee
- Somewhat pricey
- A bit difficult to prepare for the uninitated

Overall:

A unique and different type of tea that most coffee and tea lovers should try at least once.

I've been making curries for decades, in the UK and here in the USA but can't be bothered with using individual spices, so I have always used commercially available curry powder. I've always thought Sun Brand Madras Curry Powder was good - the closest I'd found in the USA to the better powders available in the UK but due to a mix-up on ordering and wanting to see if I could get a powder with a little more "heat" in it, I tried this Roland Hot Madras Curry Powder.

It says it's a Product of India but to me this is NOT curry powder! It doesn't look, smell or taste like curry - it's light brown greyish with a hint of green, doesn't have that characteristic aromatic scent of curry and it most resembles, in appearance and smell, what I once bought as Garam Masala (Rajah brand). The overriding flavor in a cooked dish is of cloves and cinnamon. Note that cinnamon is not listed in the ingredients but cassia is, though it's near the end of the list, as is cloves; possibly the ingredients are not listed in descending order of amount. The other possibilities are that the main spices are of low quality or have gone stale - wouldn't be the first time, if anyone knows the Vencatachellum-Sharwoods saga, which, from what I gather, may have undergone a further, more recent degradation. The containers are made of reinforced cardboard with a silvery inner lining and have a ring-pull aluminum seal top and bright steel bottom - no "Best By" date code so hard to tell if the product could have gone stale in storage.

For those interested in salt content, it's listed fifth in the list of ingredients but there's no "Nutrition Facts" panel so no way to know estimated amount per serving. There is no mustard, anise or ginger mentioned and interestingly, the recipe for a shrimp dish on the container mentions using fresh ginger. The rest of the ingredients look about right for a "curry powder" so I'm left wondering why I'm disappointed and what to do with those 12 cans - maybe I can blend with something to make it palatable to me. Meanwhile I'll be ordering some more Sun Brand and hoping quality hasn't deteriorated there.

Summary: Quality gourmet chocolate with no after-taste
Text:
As is, Cocoa D'Arriba consists of the best and natural ingredients only; no emulsifier, no artificial Vanillin. Concerning the high quality ingredients and business ethics, these are big pluses. However, as most reviewers have complained, there is barely any taste, let alone the fact that it is not rich or fulfilling for that matter. This is most likely due to the fact that Cocoa D'Arriba is ultra-refined (14 microns) to generate a smooth and mellow taste. That is, the chocolate is over-refined, thus very little has remained from the original rich chocolate taste. You can run into the same problem in olive oil industry, where sometimes the oil is ultra-refined during pressing, which brings about the lack of actual olive taste and thus character. Too sad.

I recommend Hachez Orange Bar 77% Cocoa instead, which is certainly a more successful product in the series. The natural orange-oil in it brings about a very mellow yet significant and pleasing orange flavor to this dark chocolate bar. It definitely adds much flavor and gives some character to this over-refined chocolate bar. It has more taste and after taste.
